rationale: Clause 16.3 caps mutual liability for property damage at US$1,000,000 while 17.1 gives an IP indemnity covering 'all litigation costs... and any damages' without stating whether it sits inside or outside that cap.
suggested_fix: Add that the indemnity in 17.1 is not subject to the US$1,000,000 limit in 16.3 (or state expressly any separate cap).

rationale: Clause 7 commits ITS to support and delivery obligations toward COMWARE's customers, yet the termination clause lets either party exit on 30 days' notice 'for any reason whatsoever' with no stated survival of those support and warranty obligations or pending purchase orders.
suggested_fix: Add that termination does not affect accepted purchase orders, warranty and support obligations for products already sold, which survive for the stated warranty period.

rationale: The Client's indemnity in clause 7 covers any Loss arising from Agent's duties except gross negligence, bad faith or wilful misconduct, while 8(a) caps Agent's liability at 24 months' fees and excludes consequential loss; the indemnity is not expressed to be subject to the cap, and 8(b) lets Agent decline to act pending judicial settlement.
suggested_fix: State that the Client indemnity applies only to Losses arising without Agent's negligence, and that clause 8(a) cap applies to Agent's liability regardless of the indemnity.

rationale: Clause 5.2 sets the timing of the awards defined in 5.1, and for cash awards defers payment to 'such later date when the outcomes of the JS incentive plans are available'.
suggested_fix: Specify a long-stop date for payment of the awards in 5.1(a) and 5.1(f) in clause 5.2.

rationale: Article V survives for ten years, but the proviso in 5.4 lets LEO and GALEN freely use confidential information after termination, which undoes the confidentiality and publicity restriction in 5.3.
suggested_fix: Limit the post-termination free-use right to each party's own information and state that the other party's confidential information stays protected for the ten-year survival period.

rationale: Clause 14.3 allows either party to terminate after a prolonged force majeure event and a 15-day consultation, while 18.4 separately terminates automatically on licence revocation outside T-Mobile's control, so two termination routes govern similar events.
suggested_fix: State in 18.4 whether licence revocation is a force majeure event and whether the 14.3 consultation and notice steps apply.

rationale: Clause 12.3 makes Customer indemnify Vendor for all Data Protection Board fines, yet 8.1 caps each party's aggregate liability at INR 15,00,000 and excludes consequential damages without carving out the indemnity.
suggested_fix: Add to 8.1 'except for Customer's obligations under Clause 12.3', or state that those obligations fall within the cap.

rationale: Section 3(c)(ii) ties termination to the Web Agreement, and Section 9 refers to 'this Section 8' while the clause is numbered 9, so the cross-references are wrong.
suggested_fix: Correct the references in Section 9 from 'Section 8' to 'Section 9' and say how disputes under the Web Agreement are resolved.

rationale: Clause 3.01 bars XSPA and its affiliates from selling competing products for six months after termination, while 5.02 makes XSPA responsible for ACDBE Partners and Franchisees, leaving unclear whether those third parties are bound by the restraint; the post-termination restraint is also void under Indian law.
suggested_fix: Limit the restraint to the Term and state whether XSPA's ACDBE Partners and Franchisees are bound by clause 3.01.

rationale: Agent's covenant in 5(c) to comply as transfer agent is expressly 'subject to Section 7', whose indemnity shifts Loss from Agent's duties to Client except for gross negligence, bad faith or wilful misconduct, so the warranty's effect depends on the indemnity.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 7 that Client's indemnity does not cover Agent's breach of its Section 5 representations, warranties and covenants.

rationale: Clause 32.6 makes third-party liabilities survive 'termination pursuant to Paragraph 18' and be shared per Schedule B, so the termination/duration mechanics in 18.1-18.2 determine when survival applies.
suggested_fix: State expressly that obligations under 32.6 survive any termination or withdrawal under Clause 18, including a single Party's exit after the Initial Period.

rationale: Section 18.4 caps Contractor's liability at amounts it actually received 'notwithstanding anything to the contrary', while Section 8 makes Customer liable for 100% of the Contract Price of cancelled products, so exposure is asymmetric and the two limits operate against each other.
suggested_fix: Make the cap in 18.4 mutual and state expressly that Customer's Section 8 payment obligations are outside the exclusion of damages.

rationale: Definition 1.11 of 'Nonconformance Notice' only has meaning through Section 3.1, which sets out the notice and acceptance procedure.

Section 6A disclaims liability for accuracy and for 'delays or interruptions ... from whatever cause' and Section 7 separately excludes all implied warranties, so overlapping exclusions invite inconsistency, and 6A also states a warranty-like assurance that no agency requirements are violated.
suggested_fix: Consolidate the exclusions in a single clause and make the express assurances in 6A 'specifically provided herein' for Section 7.

rationale: Section 1.1 defines the Group-extension and defined terms that determine who is a Licensor/Licensee Party in Section 3.1, so the licence grant only works through those definitions and the SDA.

Clause 3D lets AGI retain all royalties on termination for any reason while Section 4 makes the $1,500,000 fee non-refundable 'for any reason', so Company's early termination for AGI's material breach still leaves it unable to recover, which risks being a penalty.
suggested_fix: Make retention and non-refundability apply except where termination results from AGI's breach, with pro-rata refund in that case.

rationale: Section 3 promises a guaranteed 3-hour response and hardware service, while Section 4(a) says there 'could be an increase in service time' for listed causes without a defined relief, leaving the guarantee and exclusions imprecisely aligned.
suggested_fix: Reword 4(a) so that response-time guarantees are suspended for the listed causes for the duration of the excluded event.

rationale: Section 2.03 payment of Purchase Price relies on Company acting as agent with authority to order and accept, but Section 3.01(c) revokes that authority on termination while 3.01(a) says leased Equipment is unaffected, so pending purchases after notice are unclear.
suggested_fix: Add that Lessor remains obliged to pay for Equipment ordered and accepted before the termination date under Section 2.03.

rationale: XSPA's indemnity in 10.02 for operation of the Stores depends on 5.02/5.03, which make XSPA liable for ACDBE Partners and Franchisees' acts, extending the indemnity to third-party operators.
suggested_fix: State in 10.02 that XSPA's indemnity extends to acts and omissions of its ACDBE Partners and Franchisees under Sections 5.02 and 5.03.

rationale: The Change of Control right in 4.4 operates through the 'control' definition in Section 1.2, and the definition of 'Affiliate' with a 50% threshold fixes when termination is triggered.

Section 3.2.5 decides termination of a Workflow Development Plan 'as further described in Section 2.5', so its meaning depends on that cross-referenced procedure, while the Performance Service Plan definition is unrelated.
suggested_fix: State expressly that termination of a Workflow Development Plan is governed solely by Section 2.5 and its effect on the Performance Service Plan.

rationale: Clause 1.1 fixes the term but says the Agreement 'may be earlier terminated in accordance with the provisions hereof', so early-exit rights depend on the termination article (Section 8), which is only a heading here.
suggested_fix: Replace 'the provisions hereof' with 'Section 8 (Termination)'.

rationale: Section 7.3 lets Articles 10 (Limitation of Liability) and 11 (Arbitration) survive termination, so their continued operation depends on the survival list, though the 30-day termination for convenience cuts off payment to 'Services completed and accepted' only.
suggested_fix: Confirm in Section 7.3 that Articles 10 and 11 survive termination or expiry for all claims arising during or after the term.

rationale: Section 10.1 carves Force Majeure out of 'Supply Failure' under Section 2.13, and payment clause 5.4 incorporates License Agreement Sections 5.6.5 and 5.6.6 by reference, so both depend on provisions outside the text.
suggested_fix: State whether Force Majeure suspends Vericel's payment obligations under Section 5.4 and annex the incorporated License Agreement sections.

rationale: Section 4 makes the US Federal Arbitration Act govern all arbitration matters, while Section 5(a) says the ICC Rules prevail over the FAA in a conflict, so the clauses give different hierarchies and neither names a seat.
suggested_fix: Specify one hierarchy, for example that the ICC Rules prevail over the FAA, and name the seat and the law governing the arbitration agreement.

rationale: Clause 2 assigns 'Work Product' and 'Intellectual Property Rights' to the Company, and the latter takes its meaning from the definition in Clause 1(c).
suggested_fix: Add a definition of 'Work Product' to Clause 1 so the assignment in Clause 2 has a defined scope.

rationale: Clause 13.4 caps Supplier's liability and excludes indirect losses, but the Section 14.2 indemnity for third-party Claims is not stated to sit outside or inside that cap, so the indemnity may be undone.
suggested_fix: State in Section 13.4 whether the cap and consequential-loss exclusion apply to the Section 14.2 indemnity, for example that indemnified third-party Claims are excluded from the cap.

rationale: Clause 32.6 keeps liabilities for third-party claims after termination while Clause 33 relieves Parties for events beyond control, so liability allocation is addressed in two places, and the text of Clause 9 is about record-keeping.
suggested_fix: State that Clause 33 does not relieve the cost-sharing obligations in Clause 32.6 and Schedule B.

rationale: Section 5.1 imposes 30% liquidated delay damages forfeited from the deposit, while Section 8.2 caps Supplier's total liability at 10% of fees, and the 30% is penal and unenforceable beyond reasonable compensation.
suggested_fix: Replace Section 5.1 with a reasonable genuine pre-estimate of delay damages (for example 0.5% per week capped at 5%) and state that it counts towards the Section 8.2 cap.

rationale: Clause 6.01 allows the term to end 'unless sooner terminated' and the Agreement to be extended by consent, while 6.02 says it 'may be terminated only' on the listed grounds, which leaves expiry unaddressed and the cure periods vary in drafting.
suggested_fix: Amend 6.02 to read 'may be terminated before expiry only' and clarify that obligations incurred before termination survive.

rationale: Section 4.5 makes Article IV survive termination, which is what keeps the return or destruction duty in Section 4.4 enforceable after the Agreement ends, though no survival period is stated.
suggested_fix: Add a fixed survival period, for example 'for five years after termination, and indefinitely for trade secrets'.

rationale: Section 13.1 makes Sections 6-12 survive termination, so the return-of-Confidential-Information duty in 6.3 operates only on termination and survives through that cross-reference.

Clause 5.8 says neither party is liable for inaccuracies in Confidential Information 'under any theory of liability', but 9.1 sets a Liability Cap with carve-outs that are unclear against this blanket exclusion.
suggested_fix: State in 5.8 that the disclaimer is subject to the Liability Cap and carve-outs in Section 9.1.

rationale: Insurance clause 8(a) requires contractual liability coverage for the indemnities in Section 7, so the indemnity's practical value depends on the insurance obligations.
suggested_fix: Add that insurance limits do not cap or limit the Indemnifying Party's obligations under Section 7.

rationale: Clause 2.2 states the Appointment ends in accordance with clause 15, so the commencement clause depends on the termination clause's notice and payment-in-lieu mechanics.

Clause 12.2 carves out 'a party's indemnification obligations' from the cap, but 7.3 and the 13.1 indemnity limits (no 'other liability' for infringement) sit uneasily with the 7.2 non-infringement warranty, creating inconsistent remedies.
suggested_fix: Clarify that the 7.2 non-infringement warranty remedy is exclusively the Section 13 indemnity and is subject to the 12.2 carve-out.

rationale: The license in 2.1 runs 'during the Term' and relies on the Manufacturing Subcontractor and Tooling arrangements in Section 3 to be practically usable.

Clause 12 sends complaints to the Compliance Officer at the address notified under Clause 13.2, which works only through that cross-referenced notice clause, whose listed addresses are for general counsel not a Compliance Officer.
suggested_fix: Add the Sub-Advisor Compliance Officer's name and address in Clause 13.2 for complaints.

rationale: Marketer selection in 2.4 operates through the JPT governance process in Section 2.1 and Development Plan, so the clauses depend on each other.
Clause 18 requires written signed amendments while clause 24 separately repeats the amendment and waiver requirement, duplicating terms.
suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate amendment sentence in clause 18 and rely on clause 24.

rationale: Sick pay under 10.1 continues for 26 weeks but clause 15 allows termination on notice or payment in lieu, so entitlement during sickness depends on how termination interacts with the sick pay period.
suggested_fix: State that termination under clause 15 does not prejudice accrued sick pay entitlement under clause 10.

rationale: The guarantee forfeiture in paragraph 3 operates through paragraph 15(c) of the Agreement, and the mutual release in 5 carves out only royalties and Amendment obligations, so the release depends on the payment terms.
Survival clause 12.B keeps confidentiality surviving termination while clause 8 gives no express duration, and its 'reasonably interpreted' language leaves the period uncertain.
suggested_fix: Add an express survival period for the confidentiality obligations in Section 8.

rationale: Clause 1(a) promises Client 'preferred and dominant' reseller status, while 3(a) says Client will share Nutrition & Vitamins placements with one other reseller, which may contradict dominance.
suggested_fix: Clarify in 3(a) that sharing with another reseller is subject to Client's preferred and dominant status under 1(a).

rationale: Clause 13.2 grants exclusive rights for ten years and indefinitely on meeting minimums, while 14.9 lets the Customer sell other products only if non-competing, leaving the scope of exclusivity and the 12 right of first refusal ambiguous.
suggested_fix: Define 'non-competing products' and state that exclusivity in 13.2 is limited to Schedule A products and subject to 14.9.

rationale: Clause 34.9.3 sets the Political Event termination payment by reference to clause 37.3.2 as if an Authority Default, so its amount depends wholly on that cross-referenced formula.
suggested_fix: Restate the Political Event Termination Payment formula expressly in 34.9.3 rather than by reference.

rationale: Section 7.5 no-implied-license and 7.6 effectiveness (on Upfront Payment and Study Order approval) condition when the Section 7.1 IP and Background IP provisions take effect.
suggested_fix: Clarify that Background IP protections in 7.1(a) apply from the Effective Date irrespective of the 7.6 effectiveness conditions.

rationale: unreadable

Section 25 indemnities cover Damages broadly, while Section 26(a) bars Nexstar from consequential, special or punitive damages or lost profits when exercising Section 25(b) rights, undercutting the indemnity.
suggested_fix: State expressly whether the Section 26 exclusion of consequential damages and lost profits limits the Section 25(b) indemnity.

rationale: unreadable

Section 5.2 return-or-destroy duty with a back-up carve-out and Section 6.4 delivery of materials on termination 'subject to Section 5.2' address the same return obligation with differing wording (destroy vs deliver).
suggested_fix: Align 6.4 with 5.2 by stating that return or certified destruction satisfies the delivery obligation, subject to the back-up exception.

rationale: The indemnity in clause 13 operates over a term fixed by clause 9, whose minimum two-year term and impression-based end date determine how long indemnity exposure runs.
suggested_fix: Add that indemnity obligations in Section 13 survive expiry or termination under Section 9 for claims arising during the term.

rationale: Clause 5.4-5.6 measurement at platform facilities determines the quantities recorded in 7.2 tickets and losses deductions, so custody measurement and receipts accounting depend on each other.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer 7.2 to the measurement standards in 5.5 and state which prevails if readings differ.

rationale: Buyer Affiliates pay per the days in Attachment E, while the standard clause fixes payment at thirty days after shipment unless Attachment E says otherwise, and it adds set-off rights that the pricing clause does not mention.
suggested_fix: State that Attachment E payment days prevail over the thirty-day default and that set-off applies to the Attachment E invoices.

rationale: Clause 8 delivery of Masters 30 days before the availability date and the fee reduction for defective Masters depend on the Licensed Programs list and availability dates set under Section 2(a).
suggested_fix: Add that delivery timelines run from the availability date notified under Section 2(a) and that the 10% fee reduction is without prejudice to other remedies.

rationale: 'Aimmune Technology' is defined solely by reference to 'Aimmune Know-How' and 'Aimmune Patents' in clause 1.8, so its meaning depends on that definition.

Clause 15 allows either party to terminate without cause on 4 months' notice while clause 20.2 bars the Contractor from developing any Product for 2 years post-termination, a restraint that is void under s.27 and sits uneasily with termination at will.
suggested_fix: Limit the non-development covenant to the Term only and delete the two-year post-termination restraint.

rationale: The IP indemnity is 'without any financial limitation' while clause 7.4 caps Vendor's liability at fees paid in the prior 3 months, and it is unclear whether the cap overrides the indemnity.
suggested_fix: State expressly that the IP indemnity in 12.1 is excluded from the cap in 7.4, and that 7.4 applies only to data breach liability.

rationale: Force majeure excludes payment obligations while the price clause sets Sekisui's payment on a formula, so payment duties continue during force majeure without clear alignment.
Survival of indemnities and the Emdeon removal period in 3(c) operate alongside payment obligations in clause 4, and accrued fees and taxes are not expressly stated to survive termination.
suggested_fix: Add that accrued payment obligations under Section 4 survive expiration or termination.

rationale: Clause 14.02 keeps the assigning Party bound to confidentiality and nonuse obligations, which are defined in clause 4.02 with its 20-year term, so the continuing obligation takes its meaning from that clause.

The license grant gives Licensee VOD rights but clause 8 makes User data and Reports Confidential Information owned by Licensee, even though Licensor may request information from Licensee to gather, so the data rights are unclear.
suggested_fix: Grant Licensor a right to use Reports for royalty verification and state that any personal data is processed in accordance with the DPDP Act, 2023.

rationale: The hardware warranty requires Distributor to contact NETGEAR for an RMA number, which is detailed in clause 8 Product Returns, so the warranty remedy works only through that procedure.
suggested_fix: Add that clause 8 RMA procedure applies to warranty returns under Section 7.

rationale: JSC oversight of the Studies and its decision rights under 1.4 relate to the funding in section 4, which is tied to study budgets and enrollment targets.
unreadable
Party A may terminate if Party B fails to reach 'Party A's standards' under the Management Measures (V1.0), which are not defined here, and this interacts with the resources Party B commits in 1.6.
suggested_fix: Attach the Management Measures as a schedule and define objective termination criteria with a cure period.

rationale: The unstamped execution waiver of impounding conflicts with statutory stamping requirements, and the liability cap of 10% of fees clashes with a stated 30% penalty in Section 5.1.
suggested_fix: Delete the impounding waiver and require payment of stamp duty, and align the Section 5.1 penalty with the 8.2 cap or exclude it from the cap.

rationale: Clause 4.9 makes customs duties an element of COGS, which feeds the Available Margin formula and the true-up in clause 4.1, so price depends on tax treatment.
Section 11.1 makes the Section 8 non-compete survive termination 'for the full duration specified therein', so its enforceability depends on a post-termination restraint that is void in India.
suggested_fix: Limit survival in 11.1 to Section 6 (Confidentiality) and delete the post-termination survival of the Section 8 non-compete.

rationale: Clause 1.2.5 bars Cargill from developing succinic-acid microorganisms for the Term, while 5.2.1 reserves Cargill's right to practise Improvements 'in the field of succinic acid' for research, leaving the scope of permitted Cargill work unclear.
suggested_fix: State expressly that Cargill's reserved research use under 5.2.1 is carved out of the 1.2.5 restriction and is limited to the work under the Work Plan.

rationale: The Alternative Feedstock option modifies the Work Plan, so the 1.2.5 exclusivity and Term apply to the Modified Work Plan only through the cross-reference in clause 3.
suggested_fix: Add that the 1.2.5 exclusivity and Term extend to any Modified Work Plan once the option is exercised.

rationale: Clause 12.1 promises an IP indemnity 'without any financial limitation' notwithstanding Section 8.1, while 7.4 caps liability for data breach and regulatory matters at three months' fees, so the two liability regimes conflict.
suggested_fix: Add to 7.4 and 12.1 an express hierarchy stating which clause prevails, and that 7.4 does not limit statutory liability or the 12.1 IP indemnity.

rationale: The assistance duty in clause 4 relies on the defined terms 'Intellectual Property Rights' and 'Company Property' in clause 1 to give the further-assurance obligation its scope.

The general compensation for Authority default and the specific competing-road compensation both pay for Authority breach, and the cross-references to Clause 35.6 and 35.4 are circular and inconsistent, which invites double or disputed recovery.
suggested_fix: Correct the cross-references and state that competing-road compensation is exclusive for that breach and not additionally recoverable under the general default compensation clause.

rationale: Clause 9(a) makes the Section 8 remedies the Customer's sole remedy and caps damages at the service charge, which undercuts the 'all inclusive warranty' for 12 months in clause 2(a).
suggested_fix: Clarify that the cap in 9(a) applies to the warranty in 2(a) and state the remedies and the cap amount for the warranty period.

rationale: The Effective Date and Initial Distribution Period in the definitions feed the clause 4 renewal threshold of $45,420, and a shortfall triggers automatic termination, so the renewal clause works only through those definitions.
suggested_fix: Align the definition with clause 4 so the Initial Distribution Period is measured from the Effective Date, and provide a notice and cure step before automatic termination.

rationale: Clause 18.1 gives Bengaluru courts exclusive jurisdiction while 18.2 sends all disputes to a sole arbitrator in Bengaluru, so the forum for disputes is contradictory.
suggested_fix: Provide that disputes are finally resolved by arbitration seated in Bengaluru and that the Bengaluru courts have exclusive jurisdiction only for supervisory and interim relief under the A&C Act.

rationale: Sections 8.1 and 8.2 give near-identical IP and product-liability indemnities running in both directions, and the Company indemnity covers claims on Supplier products 'other than' those Suppliers indemnify, so the boundary invites inconsistency.
suggested_fix: Define the Company's indemnity by reference to Company-specified designs or materials and state that 8.1 takes precedence where both apply.

rationale: The Term clause survives 'any Dispute' and ends the Term via Subsection 11(d), so its termination and survival mechanics depend on the Section 11 dispute procedure.
suggested_fix: State expressly that Section 11 survives expiry or termination and that Subsection 11(d) termination is subject to completion of the negotiation and mediation steps.

rationale: The Agent's right to terminate under Section 12 changes the meaning of Section 7, which requires expense reimbursement whether or not the Conversion is completed, so the Section 2(d) cap and survival after termination must be read together.
suggested_fix: State that Section 7 reimbursement obligations survive termination under Section 12 and are subject to the Section 2(d) cap.

rationale: Clause A pays Fox a royalty on Licensee's Gross Receipts from IA2 products while B denies Licensee any share of Fox's direct-to-consumer revenues, leaving unclear whether DTC sales by Fox's assigns count as Licensee 'sale and distribution' for royalty purposes.
suggested_fix: Add: 'Revenues from Fox's direct-to-consumer channels are excluded from Gross Receipts and from any royalty or recoupment calculation under Clause 1.'

rationale: Section 5.02 makes any assignment or licence of IP subject to the 'applicable licenses, covenants and restrictions', which depend on the defined terms and confidentiality restrictions on Confidential Technical Information in the definitions section.
suggested_fix: State that any assignee or licensee must agree in writing to be bound by the confidentiality obligations for Confidential Technical Information.

rationale: Clause 2.2(b)(ii) lets the Sub-Advisor instruct the 'Custodian (as defined in Clause 5.1)' on transfers, while Clause 5.1 says the Sub-Advisor never has custody and the Custodian is selected by Oaktree US, so the delegated power works only through Clause 5.1.

Sections 3.1 and 3.2 both repeat the same 40% beneficial-ownership cap for two years after Closing, but 3.1 refers to 'HOC Entities' and 3.2 to 'HOC' for the purchase right, inviting inconsistent application.
suggested_fix: Consolidate the 40% cap into one clause applying to all HOC Entities for all Market and Private Agreement Purchases.

rationale: Section 10(a) first bars assignment without consent, then allows either party to assign to an acquirer ('Permitted Assignee'), and refers to 'Section 9(a)' and Section 3(d) of a term clause that gives Tadeo termination rights, so the change-of-control assignment may undercut those termination and extension rights.
suggested_fix: Correct the cross-reference to Section 10(a) and state that assignment to a Permitted Assignee does not affect Tadeo's termination rights under Section 3.

rationale: The final Development License Fee is payable on successful acceptance testing against an Exhibit F specification not yet agreed, and Article 6 survival of paragraphs 1-6 is tied to the termination of the Licensee's Customer Agreement rather than this agreement.
suggested_fix: Provide that Article 4 and 6 survive termination or expiry of this Agreement, and fix a deemed-acceptance date if Exhibit F is not agreed within 90 days.

rationale: unreadable
Section 10.6 makes the confidentiality provisions of Section 10, including 10.1-10.2, survive termination, which operates through the term and termination clause 11.1.

Section 2.1 sets Outsource Stepdown Rules while Article 3 begins 'Notwithstanding any other provisions' and says the Company will only 'attempt' to allocate per Section 2.1, leaving unclear which governs when they differ (largely redacted).
suggested_fix: State expressly whether Article 3 overrides the Section 2.1 allocation and Stepdown Rules, and make the allocation target binding or non-binding.

rationale: Clause 4.1 makes US$1.1 million a twenty-year payment in five instalments, while 8.3(b) requires refund of sums paid in advance for the unexpired Term on early termination, so the instalments' character as non-refundable consideration is unclear.
suggested_fix: Specify that the refund under 8.3(b) is pro-rata on the 20-year term and state the effect of termination on unpaid instalments.

rationale: unreadable
Clause 42.6 provides Article 42 survives termination, while 9.7.1 separately preserves obligations that 'expressly or by implication survive', giving two survival mechanisms that may differ in scope.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer 42.6 to 9.7.1 so that survival is governed by a single list of surviving provisions.

rationale: Clause 2.1 grants a 'perpetual, irrevocable' licence to Content and Affinities, but 2.6 limits Updating Services to the later of three events including a royalty threshold, so the perpetual licence applies to content that will become outdated without updates and the term is subject to exclusivity provisions elsewhere.
suggested_fix: State that expiry of Updating Services does not affect the perpetual licence and clarify who owns updates made by HSWI.

rationale: unreadable

Clause 13.4 caps M&I's liability 'notwithstanding any provision' but Clause 14 (Insurance and Indemnity) is a bare heading, so it is unclear whether indemnity sits inside or outside the three-month cap.
suggested_fix: State expressly whether the indemnities in Clause 14 are subject to or excluded from the liability cap in Clause 13.4.

rationale: unreadable

Cure periods differ (30 days for failing to devote best efforts versus 20 days in step-in clause E) and the force majeure carve-out in item 5 applies to closure while the step-in right does not, inviting inconsistency.
suggested_fix: Align the cure period in clause E with the 30-day cure period and state that force majeure closures do not trigger step-in.

rationale: Section 3.2 payment terms operate 'Except as provided in Section 2.1', and payments under 2.1 depend on annual reports and audit requirements defined elsewhere.
suggested_fix: Specify the due date and invoicing mechanism for Year 2 and Year 3 Quarterly Payments that are carved out of Section 3.2.

rationale: Clause 8.5 refers to arbitral proceedings and service at the Clause 9 address while Clause 9.1 only sets English law, leaving seat and curial law unclear for an arbitration.
suggested_fix: Specify the seat and governing law of the arbitration agreement expressly.

rationale: The confidentiality carve-out 5.2(d) 'as required by Applicable Law' and the Affiliates exception depend on the definitions in 1.1, including the unusual exclusion of QIWI from Affiliate.

Clause 15.1 requires 30-day cure plus 60 days' notice for default termination while 15.2 'notwithstanding anything to the contrary' allows termination at will on four months' notice, undermining the cause-based regime and warranty/quality remedies.
suggested_fix: Clarify that termination without cause under 15.2 does not affect accrued warranty and quality obligations in Clauses 9 and 10.

rationale: Clause 10.1 terminates the agreement per Fund, while 11.3 requires completion of pre-termination transactions notwithstanding termination, so it operates only through the termination trigger.

Clause A's bar on sublicensing 'except in the manner expressly provided for in Section 5.1' and the Master Territory limit operate through clause B's termination for unapproved transfers 'contrary to the terms of Section 12'.
suggested_fix: Add that termination under 10.2.3 also applies to any sublicense or management agreement made in breach of Section 1.2.

rationale: Clause A's Guarantee Forfeiture Payment is recouped from sales, while clause B's Distribution Fee deduction and remittance of the remainder to Licensee affect when and how recoupment is computed.
suggested_fix: State whether recoupment under Paragraph 3 is calculated before or after deduction of the Distribution Fee on direct-to-consumer receipts.

rationale: unreadable
The 3,000,000 guaranteed monthly Impressions in clause A are measured only through MP3.com's own logs under clause B, subject to audit and a 5% overstatement threshold for refund or credit.
suggested_fix: Specify that any shortfall against the guaranteed minimum Impressions entitles Tickets to a credit or refund, and that the audit result binds both parties.

rationale: The Content licence in clause 1(b) and the separate Marks licence in clause 5(a) both govern use of WebMD materials in the Software, with differing control terms (no change to substance without approval versus use of Marks in Emdeon's sole discretion).
suggested_fix: Make the Marks use in clause 5(a) subject to the Content restrictions and WebMD's brand guidelines in clause 1.

rationale: The consequential-loss exclusion in Section 15 expressly carves out Year 2000 compliance obligations under Section 20, so the Section 20 warranty is enforceable for consequential loss only through that cross-reference.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 15 whether the carve-out for Section 20 leaves liability uncapped or only lifts the consequential-damages exclusion.

rationale: Clause 10.1 excuses non-performance for a Force Majeure Event and imposes best-efforts and parity duties, while clause 2.5 allows PNC to terminate for failed delivery 'subject to' a Force Majeure Event without stating the interaction.
suggested_fix: State that PNC may terminate affected Purchase Orders if the Force Majeure Event continues beyond a fixed number of days.

rationale: The disclaimer in 5.2 operates through its express exception for the limited media warranty in 5.1.

The Licensor Marks licence in clause 11 and the broad Title licence in clause 2 both govern use of Licensor identifiers, with clause 11 allowing revocation for objectionable use while clause 2 sets scope limits.
suggested_fix: State that revocation of Marks under clause 11 does not affect the Title licences in clause 2.

rationale: On termination under 16.6(a), Green Cross must cease Products and transfer regulatory filings, a reversal that works through the Commercialization responsibilities and costs it assumed under clause 5.1.
suggested_fix: Specify how Commercialization costs and ongoing obligations in Section 5.1 are wound down or reimbursed upon termination.

rationale: Clause A makes the Agreement terminate automatically if the fee is not renegotiated by a Renewal Term, which conflicts with its automatic one-year renewal unless 30 days' notice is given, while the invoicing clause fixes payment on existing rates.
suggested_fix: Provide that the existing fee continues during a Renewal Term unless the parties agree otherwise, and delete automatic termination for failure to agree.

rationale: Confidentiality obligations in Section 13 continue after termination only through the survival clause 19(c), which lists Section 13.

Clause 1.2 binds NPC to comply with Visa/MasterCard Rules and is expressly 'subject to the rights of NPC to terminate pursuant to Section 6.2', which only operates when Compliance Modifications are not agreed.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 6.2 that NPC remains bound to comply with the Rules until the termination effective date.

rationale: Clause 1.02 grants an 'exclusive trade area' while 12.01 lets AIRSOPURE assign assets without liability and exit the business, leaving unclear whether the exclusivity binds an assignee.
suggested_fix: Provide that any assignee of AIRSOPURE must assume and honour the Exclusive Territory grant in writing.

rationale: The licences are stated to be 'transferable (subject to ARTICLE VIII)', so their transferability depends on Section 8.01's consent and assumption mechanics.
Service credits in 4.1 are expressly 'Subject to Section 3.2' and are triggered by shortfall against the 99.9% uptime commitment.
Termination under 10.2 and 10.3 (90-day cure, FDA loss) and force majeure termination after 60 days both give exit rights for non-performance, with differing periods and no stated precedence.
suggested_fix: State that force majeure delay is not a breach under Section 10.2 and that Section 13 governs exit for such events.

rationale: Section 16.02 prevailing-party cost recovery and 16.08 specific performance/injunction rights both govern enforcement remedies, with New York law and no defined forum.
suggested_fix: Specify the forum and clarify that Section 16.08 equitable relief is subject to 16.02 costs allocation.

rationale: Section 2(a) preferred-reseller exclusivity limiting competitor banners and Section 5 banner advertising commitments govern the same placements and could be applied inconsistently.
suggested_fix: State that Section 5 placements are counted within, and do not dilute, the prominence standard in Section 2(a).

rationale: Confidentiality obligations in Article 2 continue after termination only because Section 7.3 lists Article 2 as surviving, while 7.3 also preserves a non-compete that is void post-termination in India.
suggested_fix: Specify a fixed survival period for Article 2 and delete survival of Section 4.2 non-compete post-termination.

rationale: Royalty on Licensee's gross receipts in 2(a)(ii) and Fox's Distribution Fee on direct-to-consumer receipts in Section 4(a) both take a share of the same sales, risking double deduction.
suggested_fix: State that royalties are calculated on gross receipts net of the Distribution Fee and not charged twice on direct-to-consumer sales.

rationale: Clause 6.3 provides survival 'Notwithstanding Clause 6.2' of Clause 6 and Clauses 1, 5, 7-9, giving effect to termination under Clause 6.
Survival clause 19 preserves Sections 4-20, which carries the Section 6.1 'either during or after the Consultation Period' confidentiality duty beyond termination.
Clause 1.2 allocates first and second level maintenance and expressly relies on clause 2.2 for the incident procedure that qualifies problems before escalation to Sicap.
suggested_fix: State in clause 2.2 the response times and escalation steps that apply to second level maintenance under clause 1.2.

rationale: The Hydron termination right and four-year term in 1.2 determine how long the consideration payable under Section 3 runs, but Section 3 is only a heading here.
suggested_fix: State in Section 3 whether consideration for the post-1997 seasons is payable if Hydron terminates under 1.2.

rationale: The Section 5.1 30% delay penalty exceeds the Section 8.2 cap of 10% of fees paid, so the two cannot both be satisfied, as the clause itself notes.
suggested_fix: Align the caps by stating that delay damages under Section 5 are subject to, and count toward, the Section 8.2 cap, or carve them out expressly at a reasonable genuine pre-estimate.

rationale: The Distributor gives an uncapped indemnity in 11.1, while 13.1 caps only JRVS's liability and 13.2 cuts Distributor actions to one year, which shortens the limitation period.
suggested_fix: Make the limitations mutual, and replace the one-year bar in 13.2 with the statutory limitation period.

rationale: Clause 2.1 makes LEO bear study costs apart from GALEN's Article 3.1 obligation, while 7.4 requires GALEN to pay dues on termination, so cost allocation sits in two places.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer in 2.1 to the payments that survive under 7.4.

rationale: The IP indemnity in 12.1 is 'without any financial limitation' while 8.1 caps aggregate liability at INR 15,00,000, so the indemnity is silently undone or its uncapped nature is disputed.
suggested_fix: Add to 8.1 'except for Vendor's obligations under Clause 12.1', or state a separate super-cap for the IP indemnity.

rationale: Clause 4 bars association with any other maker of PRODUCT during the term, while Clause 6 separately restricts use of competing product in non-competitive endorsements, so the restraints overlap.
suggested_fix: State in clause 6 that it applies only during the term and is subject to the carve-outs in 4D.

rationale: Section 7.8 provides that confidentiality obligations survive termination, and 8.4 again preserves Sections 5-10 (which includes 7), duplicating the survival wording.
suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate survival wording in 7.8 or state that 8.4 governs the duration of survival.

rationale: Exclusivity under 2.1 depends on the Annual Milestones, while 4.1 separately requires commercialization milestones under Exhibit C, which may not match.
suggested_fix: State whether the Exhibit C timetable or the Section 2.1 Annual Milestones control exclusivity and termination.

rationale: Clause 3 says the Second Amendment prevails over conflicting provisions, while clause 4 ratifies the Agreement 'for all purposes and in all respects', leaving unclear which governs on a conflict.
suggested_fix: Begin clause 4 with 'Subject to clause 3,' so that the amendment prevails on any conflict.

rationale: Heading 'Inventory Balance' in 12.0 only takes meaning through 12.1's Balancing Cap return mechanism, which also cross-refers to Section 13 returns.
suggested_fix: Define the Balancing Cap percentage and measurement period explicitly and cross-refer to Section 13 returns.

rationale: Clause B deletes and substitutes Section 13.3.3, so the transfer-release text in A has no force and its meaning depends entirely on the replacement paragraph.
suggested_fix: Set out the substituted paragraph in full and state that the original 13.3.3 is superseded from the amendment date.

rationale: Service credits in 4.1 are 'subject to Section 3.2' and it is unclear whether they count toward the INR 15,00,000 aggregate cap in 8.1.
suggested_fix: State that service credits are the sole remedy for SLA failure and whether they count toward the Section 8.1 cap.

rationale: Section 2.1 grants the Village Media Company ownership of HOFV Works and a license, while 2.7 and 2.8 impose a right of first refusal and right of first offer over new PFHOF Works, so the license and pre-emption regimes cover the same subject with differing terms.
suggested_fix: Clarify whether the ROFR in 2.7 and the ROFO in 2.8 are alternatives, and how they interact with the 2.1 license and Rights Restrictions.

rationale: Section 2 provides for a four-year term with automatic one-year renewals terminable only on the Company's 90 days' notice, whereas Section 4 lets the Consultant terminate on 30 days' notice, giving two different exit regimes.
suggested_fix: Align Section 2 so that either party may give notice of non-renewal on the same period, and cross-refer expressly to the Section 4 termination rights.

rationale: unreadable

Clause 15 (inventory statement and forfeiture of the right to dispose of stock) and clause 17 (reversion of all rights on termination, with an exception 'as provided in paragraph 17' that is self-referential) both govern post-termination use and disposal of products.
suggested_fix: Correct the self-reference in 17 to cross-refer to the sell-off right and the inventory procedure in Section 15.

rationale: The definition of 'Service Levels' in 1.1 depends on the availability benchmarks in Section 3.2.

The 'as is' disclaimer of all warranties in Section 13 and the exclusion of consequential loss in Section 15 (with carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality and Y2K) both limit remedies, and the Section 20 Y2K obligations sit awkwardly against the blanket disclaimer.
suggested_fix: Add 'except as set out in Section 20 (Year 2000 compliance)' to the Section 13 disclaimer.

rationale: Section 9 termination is expressly 'except as provided in Section 10', which keeps indemnities and expense reimbursement alive after termination.

The license in Section 6.02 is granted 'to the extent of its legal right', and Section 6.07 carves out patents assigned to third parties or under exclusive licences, so the scope of the grant depends on 6.07.
suggested_fix: Make the Section 6.02 grant expressly 'subject to Section 6.07'.

rationale: Clause 1.4 refers to the place of business 'specified in Section 21.10', which is the notices address clause.
Section 9(a) makes the Section 8 repair-or-exchange warranty remedy the Customer's sole remedy, so the liability limit works only through the warranty clause, and the cap is the charge for the item.

Clause A's exclusion of consequential-type loss carves out all indemnity obligations, while B's Liability Cap carve-out covers only indemnification under Section 7.1 and material confidentiality breaches, so indemnities elsewhere stay capped and the carve-out lists differ.
suggested_fix: Align both clauses to a single carve-out list covering gross negligence, intentional misconduct, confidentiality breach and all indemnity obligations.

rationale: Section 3(b) termination relies on written notice under 8(a), which deems notice given 3 days after mailing, so the 30-day cure period depends on the notice mechanics.
suggested_fix: State that the 30-day cure period runs from deemed receipt of notice under Section 8(a).

rationale: Section 10(B) says warranties and indemnities survive termination but does not mention confidentiality, whose 3-year tail in 11.C depends on the term and is not listed as surviving.
suggested_fix: Add that Section 11 confidentiality obligations survive termination for three (3) years.

rationale: Clause A bars ABG from granting similar rights for one year after the Term, a post-term restraint of trade, and Clause B's exclusive enforcement control interacts with PAPA JOHN'S licence rights without a remedy.
suggested_fix: Limit the exclusivity restraint to the Term and drop the post-termination prohibition.

rationale: unreadable
AMAG's warranty to manufacture per Specifications, cGMP and the Quality Agreement operates through the validation protocols that 2.8 makes Antares's responsibility and subject to AMAG approval.
suggested_fix: Cross-refer 2.8 validation protocols in the 8.2 warranty.

rationale: Both clause 2 and clause 5 contain a moral rights waiver over the Work Product, duplicating the same term.
suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate moral rights waiver from Section 5 and rely on Section 2.

rationale: 3.02 excludes incidental, special or consequential damages generally while 4.01 gives an uncapped IP indemnity covering 'every expense, damage, cost and loss', leaving unclear whether the exclusion limits the indemnity.
suggested_fix: Add 'except for Company's indemnification obligations under Section 4.01' to the damages exclusion.

rationale: Clause 1 auto-renews yearly but terminates automatically if no fee agreement is reached, while clause 3 fixes an annual CPI adjustment, so a renewal can both continue with CPI-adjusted fees and automatically terminate.
suggested_fix: State that if no renegotiated fee is agreed, the CPI adjustment in Section 3 applies and the Agreement renews.

rationale: 5.1 imposes 30% of order value as liquidated damages forfeited from the security deposit for a 3-business-day delay, a penalty unenforceable beyond reasonable compensation.
suggested_fix: Replace with a reasonable genuine pre-estimate, e.g. 0.5% of order value per week of delay capped at 5%.

rationale: The Customer's indemnity for Data Protection Board fines in 12.3 is not stated to be subject to or outside the INR 15,00,000 aggregate cap in 8.1, so it is unclear whether it is capped.
suggested_fix: State in 8.1 whether the Section 12.3 indemnity is within or excluded from the cap.

rationale: The Programmer's indemnity survives termination, while clause 21 says neither party is liable for force majeure or facility upgrade failures, leaving unclear whether third-party claims arising in those events are still indemnified.
suggested_fix: Clarify that Section 21 does not limit indemnity obligations under Section 12.

citation: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, Section 8
rationale: 7.4 caps Vendor's liability for DPDPA penalties at 3 months of fees while 12.3 makes Customer liable uncapped for DPB fines from consent records, creating asymmetric and inconsistent allocation of regulatory penalties.
suggested_fix: Make penalty allocation mutual, assigning fault-based responsibility and applying a common cap to both clauses.

rationale: unreadable
The quarterly consulting fee in clause 10 triggers the 10-day payment cure period and termination rights in clause 23 on late payment.
Non-exclusive attornment to British Columbia courts sits alongside an entitlement to an 'immediate injunction' without stating which forum grants it or whether other courts may be approached.
suggested_fix: Add that either party may seek interim or injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction, including Indian courts, without prejudice to the chosen forum.

rationale: Clause 4 says the agreement 'automatically terminate[s]' if purchases fall below $45,420, while clause 7 obliges ITS to support and honour warranties and bill-back adjustments, leaving post-termination obligations unclear.
suggested_fix: Add that accrued obligations, warranty and support commitments in Section 7 survive automatic termination under Section 4.

rationale: Section 11.1 lets either party terminate on two weeks' notice, while Section 5.2 treats non-payment as material breach with a 10-day cure, so two routes exist for the same exit, and the 5.3 bonus is not addressed on termination.
suggested_fix: State how the Bonus and pro-rated Fees are treated on termination under Section 11.1 and how it interacts with the Section 5.2 breach route.

rationale: The Seller's product warranties in Section 6 are not expressly reconciled with the Section 7 indemnity for 'any actual or alleged breach of this Agreement', so warranty breaches get an unlimited third-party indemnity alongside the warranty remedy.
suggested_fix: Clarify that the Section 7 indemnity applies to warranty breaches only for third-party claims and is subject to an agreed liability cap.

rationale: Section 7 requires ITS to resolve problems 'whether or not such problems are covered under the terms of the WARRANTY', while Section 8 limits the warranty to 3 years and excludes modified or stressed equipment, so the support duty and warranty differ in scope.
suggested_fix: Clarify that the best-efforts support in Section 7 is without prejudice to, and does not extend, the Section 8 warranty exclusions.

rationale: Clause 12.1 states the agreement is executed unstamped and waives impounding, while 14.1 treats the arbitration clause as curable upon impounding, so an unstamped agreement cannot be relied on until stamp duty is paid.
suggested_fix: Delete the waiver of impounding in 12.1 and require the agreement to be duly stamped before execution or before invoking arbitration under 14.1.

rationale: Clause 11.5 requires rescission and a return to 'status quo ante' on any termination, which is unclear against the no-payment broadcast arrangement in clause 5 and what is to be unwound.
suggested_fix: Limit the clause to returning materials and state that rescission does not unwind Programs already broadcast.

rationale: Section 3(a) terminates the agreement automatically if the initial order or payment dates are missed, whereas Section 9 allows termination on 30 days' notice 'except as specifically described elsewhere', creating two inconsistent termination mechanisms.
suggested_fix: State that the automatic termination under Section 3(a) prevails over Section 9 and list the obligations that survive.

rationale: Section 9 exempts Agent from liability for events beyond its control, while Section 11(b) lets Agent suspend or terminate on non-payment, so the interaction of excused delay with Client's payment and termination rights is unaddressed.
suggested_fix: Add that force majeure does not excuse payment obligations and that prolonged force majeure gives Client a termination right.

rationale: Clause 1 puts all system, equipment and maintenance costs on the franchisee, while clause 5 separately lists installation, support and maintenance fees payable to us or a vendor that 'may be increased from time to time', duplicating the cost allocation with an open-ended fee.
suggested_fix: Specify the fees and any cap or notice period for increases, and state that clause 5 fees are the only vendor charges beyond clause 1 costs.

rationale: The amended Territory in clause 1 determines where the one-year exclusivity in clause 2 applies, and the exclusivity depends on a Marketing Plan in Exhibit 4a that is yet to be agreed.
suggested_fix: Make the Exhibit 4a Marketing Plan a condition with a fixed agreement deadline, and state the consequence if it is not agreed.
